To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the shortage of specialist homes is a consequence of the conflict between the key purpose of specialist housing, i.e. living independent, and the values that govern the production and distribution of housing in the UK.

there is a critical conflict in the UK between the social purpose of specialist accommodation (i.e. independent living) and the values underpinning the quantity of stock in both the social sector and private market.

there is a critical conflict in the UK between the key social purposes of specialist housing for older people (i.e. independent living) and the values and priorities that underpin and limit the supply of such housing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the market for specialist housing is structured and how this impacts on the availability of specialist housing.
how the market has failed the needs of older people and how the supply side of the market has failed to respond to the demand for specialist housing.
the supply side and the factors that have led to the shortage of specialist older people’s housing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specialist housing market for later life in the UK is failing older people and is in need of urgent attention.
the specialist housing market is failing older people in terms of both quality and quantity.
the UK specialist housing sector has failed older people and that the current policy environment is unlikely to change that position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UK specialist housing stock for older people is failing to meet the needs of the older population.
the UK specialist housing sector is failing older people and that it is not fit for purpose.
the specialist housing market in the UK is failing older people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current policy environment in the UK is failing to meet the housing and social care needs of an increasingly ageing population.
the specialist housing sector is not failing older people because of the lack of demand but rather because of the failure to recognise the need to supply more units.
specialist housing is not a commodity but a social good.
